answer.rationale: Blanket caveat first: every entry is a consolidated summary with the source archived, so none carry effect sizes, sample sizes, confidence intervals, segment definitions, or observation windows. I can audit only their stated claim-to-objective distance, not their underlying validity. Ratings reflect how close the claimed outcome sits to sustainable long-term qualified revenue and whether durability/harm was checked. memory_57 (4): the only entry that names qualified revenue directly AND reports an explicit retention check for harm — closest to the objective, though 'no measurable harm' may just mean underpowered, and it is scoped to established customers so it does not speak to the current SMB/activation problems. memory_44 (3): pipeline quality is a reasonable leading indicator of qualified revenue, but stops upstream of close rates, contract value, and retention; enterprise-scoped, so it is orthogonal to all three current symptoms. memory_31 (3): the word 'durable' is the only durability claim anywhere in memory, but the outcome is first-week activation — a proxy two or three steps from revenue, with no evidence the added signups were qualified rather than merely more numerous. memory_73 (2): reports revenue lift, which sounds strong, but discount-driven revenue is precisely the case where gross vs. net, margin, and post-promo churn determine whether the lift is sustainable, and none of those are recorded; it is also the memory the current competitor situation will make most tempting to over-trust, which is a reason for more scrutiny, not less. memory_86 (2): completion rate and time-to-value are operational proxies with no revenue or retention linkage and no stated duration. memory_91 (1): weakest — 'week-one engagement' and 'nudged more accounts to a first action' is the shortest-horizon, most easily-inflated proxy in the set, with no durability check, no retention check, and no revenue linkage of any kind; a nudge into a first action is fully consistent with zero long-term revenue effect. Cross-cutting gap worth flagging for the experiment decision: memory covers only wins. There are no recorded null or negative results, which is a strong signal of survivorship bias in the archive, and no memory postdates the current downturn — activation and onboarding declines are recent, so memory_91 and memory_86 may be describing effects that have already decayed or been competed away.
